lens: Task comprehension only: whether a time-constrained boutique recruiter can identify the person, dependency, source, decision, and next owned move without rereading

findings.observation: The required no-action path loses the selected person's identity. Today labels the no-action continuation as Daniel Kim, but the row passes only the no-action mode; the Session header is always derived from the global Alex Chen display name and always shows the Aurora pursuit. The resulting no-action screen therefore tells the recruiter that Alex Chen, not Daniel Kim, needs no action.
findings.evidence: Current prototype src/Prototype.tsx lines 67-77 define Daniel Kim as the no-action continuation; lines 167-174 open a Session with mode only; lines 216-218 pass the global displayName; lines 343-346 route every row without its identity; lines 367-387 render that displayName and the fixed Aurora pursuit. qa/states/no-action.png (sha256 75ed49e4ad1a50ffc400d4b4dd813294bd68fb5dbe6c16887a3b08a926526902) visibly identifies Alex Chen on the no-action state.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter cannot tell whose relationship is being held quiet and can open the wrong history. Under interruption, this is a credible relationship-state mistake rather than a cosmetic inconsistency.
findings.recommendation: Carry a typed person and pursuit identity from each Today continuation into the Session, no-action rationale, revisit condition, and history. Do not render the no-action state until all of those references resolve to the same fixture.
findings.verification: From a fresh Today state at 393x852, tap Daniel Kim. The Session header, role/pursuit, no-action explanation, revisit condition, and opened history must all identify Daniel Kim and Meridian; repeat after leaving and returning to the app.

findings.criterion: Next owned move and action payload comprehension
findings.observation: The separate approval names a local reminder, target, and time but omits the reminder title/body and the recruiter's task. The recruiter cannot see whether the reminder will prompt a remote-policy clarification, a deadline check, or something else, even though the control says “Approve exact effect.”
findings.evidence: post/approval.png (sha256 9817379699940e71963ccb4163e88a4975fbee4ff8875f3130cf900270a9e184) shows Target, When, and a generic effect only. Current prototype src/Prototype.tsx lines 520-531 define the entire approval payload; it contains no reminder title, body, or owned task. The Today dependency is “Remote policy is still unresolved” at lines 322-331, while the brief only says to confirm the deadline before planning follow-up at lines 461-465.
findings.user_impact: The flow asks for authorization before the recruiter can identify the actual work they will be reminded to do. That weakens the value exchange and can create an opaque reminder that still requires reconstructing the conversation later.
findings.recommendation: Preview the exact reminder title/body and state the owned task in relationship language, tied to the unresolved dependency and deadline. Repeat the identical content in the observed receipt.
findings.verification: On the approval screen alone, five independent recruiters can state who owns the next move, what they must do, why it matters, and when it will surface; the created reminder and receipt match that preview field-for-field.

findings.observation: At the frozen 393x852 fact state, the identity, stage explanation, and fixed decision tray consume the viewport; neither the unresolved dependency nor the quoted WhatsApp source is visible beside the Unknown → Wed, Sep 2 decision. The screen says the exact source stays visible, but the recruiter must scroll the underlying page and then return to the decision controls.
findings.evidence: post/fact.png (sha256 d9d4e6fa7606a69d31657448b48318baa25221e1c2d06adc5e1ea3a83d1fe86e) shows the fact decision without its source or dependency. Current prototype src/prototype.css lines 136-181 place the stage panel, dependency, source, and brief in the scrolling page, while lines 181-183 reserve 388px and fix a 370px decision tray over the bottom of the viewport.
findings.user_impact: The recruiter must hold or reconstruct the evidence-to-fact relationship at the moment of confirmation, which fails the dimension's “without rereading” standard and encourages superficial confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Keep a compact source excerpt and dependency adjacent to the proposed fact in the decision viewport, or collapse the explanatory stage panel so evidence and decision are simultaneously readable.
findings.verification: A fresh 393x852 fact capture shows person, pursuit, unresolved dependency, source channel/time and exact quote, proposed state change, and all three fact decisions without scrolling or occlusion.

strengths: The Today lead directly names Alex Chen, the Aurora role, the unresolved remote-policy dependency, the Wed Sep 2 decision date, the WhatsApp source and timestamp, and the existence of a separate effect review.
The Fact → Effect → Outcome rail makes the decision sequence legible, and the fact tray offers Confirm, Edit, and Not supported rather than forcing acceptance.
The standalone no-action copy is restrained and supplies a revisit condition instead of manufacturing urgency; the defect is the routed identity, not the no-action concept.
missing_evidence: No freeze-candidate.json identifies the exact candidate source and screenshot hashes. The current Prototype.tsx and prototype.css hashes differ from freeze-baseline.json, and the post captures predate the latest source timestamps.

The evaluation bundle has no frozen no-action capture reached through its Today continuation; the available no-action screenshot is in the prototype QA directory, so route behavior is evidenced primarily by current code.
No blinded real-recruiter comprehension result is present; the bundle README says the separate two 9/10 human comprehension tests remain pending.
vetoes: Active: the effect labeled “exact” can enter execution without showing the reminder content or owned task, so the consequential write is not fully scoped for recruiter approval.
open_questions: What exact reminder title/body is created and later read back?
Is the frozen no-action fixture intended to be Daniel Kim/Meridian or Alex Chen/Aurora?
Which post or tightened Today capture is the canonical candidate when freeze-candidate.json is absent?
